findings.title: Do not let the view scope authorize global group management
findings.body: The parameterless canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on all groups. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() relies on this check through requireManage(), so an administrator granted only read access can POST to create groups or move an existing group to the realm root by supplying its ID. This also contradicts canManage(GroupModel), which requires MANAGE. The global management check must require MANAGE, with a regression test denying these operations to a VIEW-only administrator.

findings.title: Collect actual group IDs for member searches and counts
findings.body: groupResource.getId() is an authorization-resource UUID, not the GroupModel ID. Individual resources are named with the group ID by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(), and that method does not assign them the Groups type either. Consequently, this loop misses individual group permissions and, when an all-groups member permission is granted, returns the all-groups authorization UUID as a group ID. UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource pass these IDs to membership-filtered queries, causing authorized users to disappear from searches and producing incorrect counts. Enumerate actual group IDs and explicitly handle all-groups grants.

findings.title: Enable delegated group-member creation for V2
findings.body: The group-member creation fallback still accepts only the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ V1 feature. With only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, an administrator granted MANAGE_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP on a group cannot create a user assigned to that group: requireManage() rejects the administrator's lack of global user-management permission, and this feature check immediately disables the fallback before consulting the new group evaluator. Allow the fallback under V2 as well and test creation using only the two group scopes.

findings.title: Provision the new schema entries for existing permissions clients
findings.body: Adding Groups to the static schema does not install its resource or scopes into an already-initialized V2 realm, because init() returns immediately when the realm has an admin-permissions client. Such realms retain the previous Users/Clients schema and lack manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members. Creating their first group permission calls getOrCreateResource(), which attempts to attach every Groups scope and throws ModelException("No scopes found."). Synchronize the new schema entries for existing clients rather than provisioning them only when the client is first created.
